Q: How does OSX Activity Monitor match XPC tasks to their initiator process? A:

It seems that activity monitor groups processes for application using responsible process id which could be retriven using this command:

sudo launchctl procinfo <pid> | grep responsible

Q: C++ Best way to get integer division and remainder A: 
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main()
{       register unsigned a = random(), b = random();
        printf("%u %u\n", a / b, a % b);
        return 0;
}

gcc -O3 -masm=intel -S -o - divrem.c

        .file   "divrem.c"
        .intel_syntax noprefix
        .text
        .section        .rodata.str1.1,"aMS",@progbits,1
.LC0:
        .string "%u %u\n"
        .section        .text.startup,"ax",@progbits
        .p2align 4,,15
        .globl  main
        .type   main, @function
main:
.LFB22:
        .cfi_startproc
        push    rbx
        .cfi_def_cfa_offset 16
        .cfi_offset 3, -16
        call    random
        mov     rbx, rax
        call    random
        xor     edx, edx
        mov     rcx, rax
        mov     eax, ebx
        div     ecx
        mov     edi, OFFSET FLAT:.LC0
        mov     esi, eax
        xor     eax, eax
        call    printf
        xor     eax, eax
        pop     rbx
        .cfi_def_cfa_offset 8
        ret
        .cfi_endproc
.LFE22:
        .size   main, .-main
        .ident  "GCC: (SUSE Linux) 7.5.0"
        .section        .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits

GCC 7.5.0

I used random cause any constant division will done by the compiler and no division instruction at all will be executed !!!

As you can see, there's a single division instruction (which yields both the division result and the remainder). GCC picks up both results and push into the stack for printf.

ARM require a division followed by a multiplication/subtraction instruction to get the remainder. gcc does it automatically.

Q: HTML DIV Styles / Layout A:

I would recommend a div wrapper as a two column Grid, and the content on the right as another Grid. When full display, show 2 columns in the main div and the same with the content. When the page resizes you can change the columns to 1, so it rearranges content. How's your CSS skills?

Q: How to fix "Unresolved reference 'outlinedTextFieldColors'" for TextFieldDefaults? A:

You haven't shared which Jetpack Compose version you are using, but it seems like you are trying to use a deprecated and subsequently deleted API.

From Compose BOM 2024.09.00 onwards, you need to use the OutlinedTextFieldDefaults.colors instead of TextFieldDefaults.outlinedTextFieldColors.

For example:

OutlinedTextField(
    value = task,
    onValueChange = { task = it },
    label = { Text("Anexe uma tarefa") },
    colors = OutlinedTextFieldDefaults.colors(
        focusedTextColor = Color.Black,
    ),
)

Note that the composable method colors has many more arguments you can use:

@Composable
fun colors(
    focusedTextColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    unfocusedTextColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    disabledTextColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    errorTextColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    focusedContainerColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    unfocusedContainerColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    disabledContainerColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    errorContainerColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    cursorColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    errorCursorColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    selectionColors: TextSelectionColors? = null,
    focusedBorderColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    unfocusedBorderColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    disabledBorderColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    errorBorderColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,

Q: Split the legend into three rows with headings for a nested facet_wrap A:

As suggested by @r2evans in the comments, the legendry package now offers an easy out-of-the-box option to

keep groups in blocks with their own titles

via guide_legend_group:

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggh4x)
library(legendry)

df0 |>
  filter(analyte == select_analyte) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year_month, y = cv, group = analyzer)) +
  ggtitle(paste0(select_analyte)) +
  facet_wrap2(
    vars(qc, site),
    ncol = 3,
    drop = FALSE,
    strip = strip_background
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = 0.05)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1)),
    breaks = breaks_pretty()
  ) +
  geom_line(
    # Add the subgroup name and the seperator = "." used to split into
    # groups
    aes(color = paste0(site, ":.", analyzer)),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression("cv")) +
  theme(
    plot.margin = unit(c(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 0.5), "cm"), # trbl
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", vjust = 1),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, vjust = 1),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "grey10", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    strip.background = element_rect(color = "black", linetype = "solid"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 13, color = "black"),
    strip.text.y = element_text(size = 13, color = "black", angle = -90),
    axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = -0.5, size = 13),
    axis.title.y = element_text(vjust = 4.8, size = 13),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      margin = margin(b = 0.1),
      hjust = 1.12, vjust = 1.05, colour = "black", size = 10, angle = 60
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      margin = margin(l = -5, r = 2.5),
      colour = "black", size = 12
    ),
    legend.margin = margin(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.direction = "vertical"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend_group(
    key = key_group_split(sep = "\\."),
    override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.3),
    nrow = 1,
    title = NULL
  )) +
  theme(
    legendry.legend.subtitle.position = "left",
    legendry.group.spacing = unit(0, "cm")
  )

A second option would be the ggnewscale package which however requires much more effort and as downside does not align the legend keys in columns across the legend groups:

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggh4x)
library(ggnewscale)

df1 <- df0 |>
  filter(analyte == select_analyte)

# per site color palettes
pal_color <- df1 |>
  distinct(site, analyzer) |>
  arrange(site, analyzer) |>
  mutate(
    color = scales::pal_hue()(n_distinct(analyzer))
  ) |>
  split(~site) |>
  lapply(
    function(x) {
      x |>
        select(-site) |>
        deframe()
    }
  )

# plot
df1 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year_month, y = cv, group = analyzer)) +
  ggtitle(paste0(select_analyte)) +
  facet_wrap2(
    vars(qc, site),
    ncol = 3,
    drop = FALSE,
    strip = strip_background
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = 0.05)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1)),
    breaks = breaks_pretty()
  ) +
  purrr::imap(
    df1 |> split(~site),
    function(x, site) {
      list(
        geom_line(data = x, aes(color = analyzer), linewidth = 1),
        scale_color_manual(
          values = pal_color[[site]],
          guide = guide_legend(
            title = paste0(site, ":"),
            override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.3),
            order = which(names(pal_color) == site)
          )
        ),
        ggnewscale::new_scale_color()
      )
    }
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression("cv")) +
  theme(
    plot.margin = unit(c(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 0.5), "cm"), # trbl
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", vjust = 1),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, vjust = 1),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "grey10", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    strip.background = element_rect(color = "black", linetype = "solid"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 13, color = "black"),
    strip.text.y = element_text(size = 13, color = "black", angle = -90),
    axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = -0.5, size = 13),
    axis.title.y = element_text(vjust = 4.8, size = 13),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      margin = margin(b = 0.1),
      hjust = 1.12, vjust = 1.05, colour = "black", size = 10, angle = 60
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      margin = margin(l = -5, r = 2.5),
      colour = "black", size = 12
    ),
    legend.margin = margin(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.box.just = "left",
    legend.spacing = unit(0, "pt")
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")

Q: How to fix 'SQLite exception, Insufficient parameters supplied to the command' when using INSERT statement A:

Perhaps the following tip will help someone. I had this problem when updating to version 1.0.118 of System.Data.Sqlite. From this version onwards, the parameters are case-sensitive:

SQLiteCommand command = 
      new SQLiteCommand(“insert into bridge (id, engWord) values (@id, @engWord)”,cnn);

This does not work:
command.Parameters.AddWithValue(“engword”, br.engWord)

This works:
command.Parameters.AddWithValue(“engWord”, br.engWord)

Q: Code changes are not applied when running docker container A:

If you're using a simple dockerfile you have to rebuild and rerun the docker container in order to see the changes made to the source.

You can think of a docker container as an immutable snapshot, once they're built they're not attached to the source code or other external factors.

This way it becomes self-contained by encapsulating all dependencies and isolated from external environment by default, this is great for reproducibility and thus great for deploying the app later and resolve the #worksOnMyMachine problem.

From docker.

What is a container? Simply put, containers are isolated processes for each of your app's components. Each component - the frontend React app, the Python API engine, and the database - runs in its own isolated environment, completely isolated from everything else on your machine.

Q: confluent kafka producer KafkaError{code=_MSG_TIMED_OUT,val=-192,str="Local: Message timed out"} A:

You need to get more logs. The code below helped me a lot. You may need to wait up to 5 minutes till the logs appear.

from logging import getLogger, DEBUG
from confluent_kafka import Producer


logging.basicConfig(level=DEBUG)
logger = getLogger(__name__)


conf_dict = {
    'bootstrap.servers': <bootstrap server>,
    ...,
    # the two lines below did the trick, both are needed
    'logger': logger,
    'debug': "broker,topic,metadata"
}

producer = Producer(conf_dict)
producer.produce(topic="my_topic", key="some_key", value="some_value")
producer.poll(0)
producer.flush()
